commands.author: lzyyzznl

target.title: fix: tighten readSchema.limit from Type.Number to Type.Integer
target.body:
## Summary

**Problem**: `readSchema.limit` accepts floating-point values via `Type.Number()` while the sibling field `offset` already correctly uses `Type.Integer({ minimum: 1 })`. This inconsistency means an LLM can pass `limit=10.5` and get 10 lines back instead of the expected 10-11.

**Solution**: Tighten `limit` to `Type.Integer()` — matching the same schema's `offset` field. TypeBox rejects float values at the parameter parsing stage, before reaching runtime.

**What changed / NOT changed**: Three changes in `src/agents/sessions/tools/read.ts`:
1. Schema: `Type.Number()` → `Type.Integer()` on the `limit` property
2. Runtime: Added `Number.isSafeInteger` validation for `limit` in the execute function (matching the existing `offset` validation pattern)
3. Added focused regression test file `src/agents/sessions/tools/read.limit-schema.test.ts` (8 test cases covering both schema layer and execution boundary against the actual production schema via `createReadToolDefinition`)

The runtime `Number.isSafeInteger` guard rejects non-integer limit values at the tool-call boundary, matching `offset`'s existing validation. `normalizePositiveLimit` handles the actual value clamping. No config, CLI, or public API surface changed. No dependencies added or updated. This is a consistency fix aligning `limit` with the already-correct `offset` field.

**merge-risk declaration**: No — schema-only change to an internal tool schema type. No session state, auth, message delivery, or security boundary involved.

## Real behavior proof

**Behavior addressed**: Two-layer validation — (1) schema-level `Type.Integer` rejects float values at the TypeBox parameter parsing stage, (2) tool execution boundary `Number.isSafeInteger(limit)` rejects non-integer limit at runtime.

**Real environment tested**: Linux x86_64 (local workstation)

**Exact steps or command run after this patch**: Two-layer validation against the actual production `readSchema` (from `createReadToolDefinition`):

```
$ npx tsx _validate.mts

=== Layer 1: Schema validation (Value.Check) ===
  ✓ valid int limit:           {"path":"/tmp/x","limit":100} → true
  ✓ float limit — rejected:   {"path":"/tmp/x","limit":3.14} → false
  ✓ valid offset (sibling):   {"path":"/tmp/x","offset":1} → true
  ✓ limit omitted (opt):      {"path":"/tmp/x"} → true
  ✓ missing required path:    {"limit":10} → false

=== Layer 2: Execution boundary validation ===
  ✓ float limit — rejected with: "Limit must be an integer"
  ✓ valid int limit — execution succeeded
✅ All validation checks passed — float limit rejected at both schema and execution boundary.
```

Focused regression tests (8/8):
```
$ vitest run src/agents/sessions/tools/read.limit-schema.test.ts
 ✓ read tool limit schema (production) > accepts valid integer limit
 ✓ read tool limit schema (production) > rejects float limit at schema layer
 ✓ read tool limit schema (production) > accepts omitted limit (optional)
 ✓ read tool limit schema (production) > accepts valid integer offset (sibling field)
 ✓ read tool limit schema (production) > still validates required path
 ✓ read tool limit execution boundary > rejects float limit at execution boundary
 ✓ read tool limit execution boundary > accepts valid integer limit at execution boundary
 ✓ read tool limit execution boundary > accepts non-positive integer limit (clamped at runtime)
 Tests  8 passed (8)
```

**After-fix evidence**: Float values rejected at TWO layers — `Value.Check()` returns `false` at schema layer, and `tool.execute()` throws `"Limit must be an integer"` at the execution boundary. Valid integers and omitted optionals pass. All 8 regression tests pass.

**Observed result after the fix**: Float values correctly rejected by both schema layer and execution boundary. Valid integer values, omitted optional, sibling `offset`, and non-positive integer limits (clamped at runtime) continue to work.

**What was not tested**: End-to-end LLM read tool invocation through the Gateway agent runtime. The tool-call boundary is validated via direct `tool.execute()` calls with mock operations, covering both schema rejection and execution-time rejection.

## Tests and validation

- `pnpm build:ci-artifacts` → exit 0 ✓ (compilation succeeds with new schema type)
- `pnpm test vitest.agents-tools.config.ts` → exit 0, 54 passed ✓ (agents tools tests pass, including read tool related tests)
- Focused regression: `vitest run src/agents/sessions/tools/read.limit-schema.test.ts` → 8/8 passed ✓
  - Schema layer: valid int, float rejection, optional, sibling offset, required path (5 tests)
  - Execution boundary: float rejection, valid int, non-positive integer clamped (3 tests)
  - All tests validate against actual production schema from `createReadToolDefinition`
- Baseline: 3 pre-existing test failures (auth/OpenAI credentials, unrelated to this change)

## Risk checklist

- [x] This change is backwards compatible — existing callers passing integer values work identically; callers passing floats now get a clear validation error at both schema layer and execution boundary
- [x] This change has been tested with existing configurations — built and tested with default config
- [ ] I have updated relevant documentation — not needed, internal schema type change with no user-visible surface
- [ ] Breaking changes (if any) are documented in Summary — no breaking changes
